summary: Reviewed the submitted nan_to_num_ candidate (.best_kernel.py, sha256 bc15a973… = ledger round-3 solution and the subject under review) against the frozen catalog contract (definition.json / evaluation-contract.json / correctness.jsonl / timing.jsonl / oracle.py) and the round history and measurements in .ledger.json, optimize_definition_output.json and the review_tests artifacts. The candidate is a genuine self-contained Triton in-place pass: `run(A, nan=None, posinf=None, neginf=None)` mutates A's storage and returns A, matching `mutates: [A]` / `returns_alias_of: {out: A}` (definition.json:32-39); it uses no torch.ops/torch fallback, no host synchronization, no .item()/.cpu(), no environment mutation and no test-specific shapes or magic values (block sizes are dtype/size-driven). The saturating-clamp selection (element_size()==2 and posinf>=finfo.max and neginf<=finfo.min) is an algebraically valid simplification, but the graded set never exercises its complement: all correctness cases pass nan=0., posinf=None, neginf=None (oracle.py:43-44) and all timing inputs are plain randn with no NaN/±Inf (timing.jsonl:1-12), so the fast=False branch and the fp32-staged replacement values are unvalidated, and 6 of 18 'special' correctness cases (shape [1], numel<7) contain no special values at all because the edge-value injection is gated on numel>=7 (oracle.py:20-23; correctness.jsonl:1-2,7-8,13-14). Static review found no wrong-implementation measurement or reference-circularity issue; per the supplied evidence (evaluate.json / optimize_definition_output.json) the candidate passed 18/18 correctness and 12/12 timing with abs/rel error 0.0, and the ledger records 30/30 PASSED. The substantive code concerns are: (a) the cached direct Triton launcher bypasses Triton's per-call specialization checks (pointer alignment/divisibility) and is keyed only by (dtype, numel, fast) with no device key, so a second NPU could launch on device-0's cached stream; (b) reliance on private torch_npu/Triton launch internals with no guard at launch time, so a failure raises instead of using the documented fallback; (c) complex inputs silently no-op; (d) overlapping (expanded/stride-0) views silently succeed where the reference raises. Performance note (not a defect): in the authoritative final verification the delivered candidate is slower than the reference on all 12 timing workloads (geo_mean 0.6513; per-workload speedup ≈0.53-0.73, e.g. timing-3 0.0576 ms vs reference 0.0305 ms), so the PASSED status is a correctness gate, not a speedup over the baseline.

findings.evidence: .best_kernel.py:187-202 (_try_build warms up with the first caller's tensor A and caches launcher.launch/ck.function/ck.packed_metadata), .best_kernel.py:254-262 (entry cached under key (A.dtype, n, fast) and then invoked with a raw A.data_ptr(), bypassing JITFunction.run's per-call binder). .ledger.json:1252-1279 round-3 solution = subject sha256 bc15a973….
findings.reason: Triton's launcher cache key includes pointer specialization (16-byte divisibility) computed from the actual tensor passed at call time. The candidate freezes one compiled variant per (dtype, numel, fast) from the warmup tensor and thereafter passes only an int pointer, so a contiguous tensor with a non-16-byte-aligned storage offset (e.g. a float16/float32 slice such as x[1:], which is contiguous and therefore takes this path at .best_kernel.py:250-253) would be launched with a kernel compiled under the warmup pointer's alignment assumption; Triton would instead have selected/recompiled an unspecialized variant. This is a silent mis-launch hazard for valid inputs outside the graded set (the graded tensors are fresh, allocator-aligned, so the evidence does not contradict the 18/18 PASSED result).
findings.requested_change: Either include the pointer divisibility (data_ptr() % 16) in the entry key and re-resolve when it changes, or keep the cached launch only for the confirmed-aligned case and route everything else through the ordinary kernel[grid](...) path. Document the alignment precondition next to the cache.

findings.evidence: .best_kernel.py:199-200 (entry stores _resolve_stream(A.device.index or 0)), .best_kernel.py:254-262 (cache key is (A.dtype, n, fast); entry[5] is the stream getter bound at build time), .best_kernel.py:141-184 (_STREAM is keyed per device but the launch entry is not).
findings.reason: The launch entry carries a stream getter resolved for the device of the first caller only, and the entry key contains no device index. A tensor with the same dtype and numel on a second NPU would reuse that entry and enqueue the work on the first device's current raw stream, which is a wrong-stream (and potentially wrong-context) launch rather than a re-resolution. The graded harness is single-device (evaluate.json:5 "device": "npu:0"), so this is latent rather than observed.
findings.requested_change: Add the device index to the _ENTRIES key (or store the device in the entry and resolve the stream from the entry's own device plus a per-call re-check), so multi-device use cannot reuse a foreign stream.

findings.evidence: .best_kernel.py:30-36 (docstring promises 'Any build failure falls back to the validated staged kernel, and from that to the ordinary kernel[grid](...) launch'), .best_kernel.py:152-154 (import torch_npu + private torch_npu._C._npu_getCurrentRawStreamNoWait), .best_kernel.py:259-262 (bare call to entry[0](...) with a hand-built 9+6 positional argument list, including the trailing constexpr block as an extra argument).
findings.reason: The fast path depends on private, version-specific internals on two sides (torch_npu's raw-stream accessor and Triton's internal launcher signature, where the trailing BLOCK value only works because the generated launcher ignores arguments beyond the non-constexpr parameter count). The try/except protection ends at build time (.best_kernel.py:190-202); any ABI drift that only manifests when `launch` is called raises out of run() instead of falling back as the docstring states, and the check for msprof/debug flags is also only made once at build time, so a later profiling mode change cannot disable the bypass.
findings.requested_change: Wrap the direct launch in a try/except that permanently marks the entry unusable and re-dispatches through _nan_to_num_stage[grid](...) on failure; obtain the stream from a public API where one exists; and document the exact Triton launcher ABI the positional call assumes.

findings.evidence: .best_kernel.py:269-271 (`if not A.is_floating_point(): return A`), oracle.py:75-76 (reference is `A.nan_to_num_(nan, posinf, neginf)`), definition.json:4-39 (no dtype restriction in the frozen contract).
findings.reason: torch's nan_to_num_ is defined for complex tensors (replacing NaN/±Inf in real and imaginary parts), but the candidate silently returns a complex tensor unchanged because is_floating_point() is False for complex64/complex128. That is a silent no-op divergence from the reference on a dtype the frozen Definition does not exclude. No graded case covers complex (correctness.jsonl:1-18 uses only float16/bfloat16/float32), so this is advisory for the graded set but would be a wrong answer if the dtype set ever widens.
findings.requested_change: Handle complex by applying the transform to real and imaginary parts (e.g. via view_as_real semantics) or explicitly raise NotImplementedError for complex rather than returning the input unchanged, and note the supported dtype set in the module docstring.

findings.evidence: .best_kernel.py:217-247 (_launch_strided keeps every non-size-1 axis, including stride-0 axes, in `dims`; .best_kernel.py:96-116 computes one offset per element and stores without any overlap check), .best_kernel.py:231-236 / 243-247 (scaled and ND kernels used for such views).
findings.reason: For an expanded/broadcast view (a size>1 axis with stride 0) the candidate keeps the stride-0 axis and lets several lanes write the same storage slot, so the call silently succeeds. PyTorch's in-place TensorIterator path rejects writes that alias a single memory location and raises for such tensors, so the candidate both skips a reference error and silently produces a (numerically benign, last-writer-wins) buffer. This layout is not covered by the graded set (the `strided` inputs are constructed as base[..., 0], oracle.py:24-27, which has a uniform non-zero stride).
findings.requested_change: Detect stride-0 (overlapping) axes and either raise as the reference does or fall back to a host-side/1-element-per-slot formulation; add a targeted note that overlapping views are out of scope if raising is chosen.

findings.evidence: oracle.py:19-23 (edge values injected only when `s.get('special') and x.numel() >= 7`), oracle.py:43-44 (all nan_to_num_ inputs use `nan=0., posinf=None, neginf=None`), correctness.jsonl:1-2,7-8,13-14 (shape [1] cases with special=true), .best_kernel.py:279-290 (the fast/general branch split).
findings.reason: 6 of the 18 graded correctness cases are labelled special but contain only a single random value, so they exercise no NaN and no ±Inf at all. In addition the graded contract never supplies a non-default nan/posinf/neginf, so the fast=False branch (fp32-staged compare/select at .best_kernel.py:51-58/83-92/96-116, plus the fp32→fp16/bf16 cast of posinf/neginf) is validated only by the default saturating arguments. This is a limitation of the frozen source test design, not of the candidate, so it is recorded as advice for pytest review.
findings.requested_change: For the source-test owner (not the extractor): include at least one case per dtype with a small numel but a 2-D shape (so the >=7 gate fires), and one case per dtype with explicit finite posinf/neginf (and non-zero nan) to cover the non-saturating replacement branch.

findings.evidence: timing.jsonl:1-12 (every timing spec omits `special`, so oracle.py:20-23 injects no edge values and x stays torch.randn), oracle.py:43-44 (default arguments only), optimize_definition_output.json:8-212 (round-3/final ratios).
findings.reason: Every timed workload runs over data that contains no NaN and no ±Inf and uses the default replacement arguments, so the replacement selects and the clamp branch are never taken on a live lane; the measured 83.4→57.6 us fp16 4096x4096 gain (.ledger.json:2040-2041) reflects a branch-free clamp over plain random data. Correctness/бaseline separation is intact (candidate and reference see identical inputs), but the timings do not measure the cost of the actual replacement path. Source-test limitation, recorded as advice.
findings.requested_change: For the source-test owner: add at least one timing spec that carries the `special` flag so NaN/±Inf lanes are present in the timed input, keeping the same seed/shape so the comparison stays apples-to-apples.

findings.evidence: .ledger.json:2031-2036 (round 3 profile status "failed": msprof base collection exited without a profile completion marker across 6 attempts, artifacts [], metrics {}, capabilities []), .best_kernel.py:193-198 (the direct-launch path deliberately declines launchers with msprof registration enabled).
findings.reason: No per-kernel device evidence exists for this round, so the device-side claims about the clamp tile rest on separate debug measurements quoted in the docstring/ledger (.best_kernel.py:20-22) rather than on a collected profile. This is a profiler availability limitation of the target environment, recorded for downstream readiness; it is not caused by the candidate (the bypass is only used when the msprof flag is absent, and otherwise returns _FAIL and falls back).
findings.requested_change: Record the profiler unavailability as a known target limitation and, when profiles are needed again, verify that the direct-launch bypass is disabled (i.e. _try_build returns _FAIL) so msprof instrumentation is collected.
